title: Count pair sums
prompt:
A ticket system logs integer badge numbers. Return how many index pairs (i, j) with i < j satisfy values[i] + values[j] == target.

- values has 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^9 and 10^9; target is in the same range.
- Equal values at different indices form different pairs.
- Return an integer. Do not modify values.
hints: A brute-force double loop is O(n²). What would you need to know, at index j, to count its partners instantly?
Partners of values[j] are earlier values equal to target - values[j]. Keep a count of every value seen so far.
For each value: add count[target - value] to the answer, then increment count[value]. Updating after the lookup stops a value pairing with itself.

solution.explanation: Scan left to right with a frequency map of values already seen. Every earlier value equal to target - value completes a pair with the current index, so add that count before recording the current value. Each pair is counted exactly once, at its right-hand index.

complexity.notes: One pass with expected O(1) hash operations. The answer can reach n(n-1)/2 (about 5·10^9), which still fits exactly in a JavaScript number.

followUps: How would you count pairs if values arrived as a stream too large to keep in memory?
What changes if the question asks for pairs with a difference of exactly target?
